body: Holy crap it deleted all my documents. WTF
EPIC FAIL

And now I'm trying to restore the files that have gone missing on the local machine, I've left syncthing running and it's deleting the new files as they get added. I even tried adding a brand-new text file and it deleted that too. I have two questions:
1. How do I make it work?
2. How can I ever trust this tool again?

I've been waiting for a tool like this and I'm so utterly disappointed.

If you're wondering, I followed the install / setup instructions at http://discourse.syncthing.net/t/getting-started/46 and then poked around the web-ui adding nodes and repositories. I'm not aware of having done anything unexpected. My machines are pretty clean installs.

If I can do anything to help anyone else avoid this problem let me know.

The only time syncthing deletes items is when it gets an update from another node marking a file or directory as deleted. This happens when syncthing has seen a file, does a rescan, and then it is no longer there (i.e. it has been deleted).
Hmmm, does it move files to trash (if trash is found on the system) or does it delete them completely? This way it could get more trustworthy.
Nothing in my trash.

> The only time syncthing deletes items is when it gets an update from another node marking a file or directory as deleted.

Well what-ever the reason the end result is all my files are gone. I though you might like to know about this as it seems like a bit of a critical bug to me. Personally I have backups, but others might not be so lucky.

If anyone wants me to collect any evidence to help prevent this ever happening again before I throw my computer(s) out the window then please do let me know.

Just been reading http://discourse.syncthing.net/t/syncthing-on-nas-arm-v5-almost-solved/55/9

Could this epic screw-up be because the second machine had a symlink for Documents to another disk?

Yes, that would probably do it. We can create Documents/foo, but on rescan we won't see it any more, so it will have been "deleted".

Possibly we should throw an error when we find symlinks in the repository.
Oh, and sorry for the inconvenience, obviously. :( Beta software, new situation. :/

No problems, I consider all open source to be in beta anyway and I did see the big pre-1.0 warning. I appreciate the creation of this tool and am really only trying to help out even if I was a bit annoyed.

I think that for the root of a repository syncthing should just follow the symlink. For symlinks inside a repository I'd just copy the symlink itself by default personally.

A couple of features unison has that would be worth considering:
- You can choose whether symlinks inside a repository should be followed and the contents synced, or copied verbatim. Obviously this has issues on windows.
- If unison notices an entire tree is missing it will throw a warning rather than automatically deleting everything. In the UI the user can choose to continue (unison-gtk). I suggest this would be a suitable mitigation for this bug.
Agreed, those are some good points. Obviously as it is now it's dangerous. There are some corner cases to sort out. #92 is the main ticket. Following-and-flattening is probably the easiest to handle.

rename.to: All files deleted on first sync if repo root is symlink

body:
Note to self and potential other readers: the same will happen when doing initial sync of two pre-populated repositories where one side has a folder and the other has a symlink. I.e.;

## Side A

```
repoRoot/
    foo/
        somefile
```

## Side B

```
repoRoot/
    foo -> /somewhere/else
```

On first sync, side B will create `repoRoot/foo/somefile` (actually `/somewhere/else/somefile`). On the next scan, since we don't follow symlinks, the entire `repoRoot/foo` directory will be "gone" and marked as deleted. Side A will then delete the files. (They might still be on side B, I'm not sure.)

Sounds good. I agree with the description you've posted. I'm currently re-running the sync without any symlinks in the path so I'll let you know if anything comes up. (13gb over 100mbit lan so will take a while).

Thanks for your speedy responses. I now <3 this project again :-)

Here's a particular use case for symlinks that I personally make use of:
- /home on small primary ssd
- /home/tim/Music starts off on ssd
- /home/tim/Music gets too big for ssd
- Move Music folder to /media/bigdisk/Music
- create symlink /home/tim/Music -> /media/bigdisk/Music
- expect all programs to not notice.

In the current situation syncthing will think it's now empty and delete everything from all other replicas -> sadface.

FYI the latest sync of Documents this time without a symlink seems to be behaving so it looks like the symlink is indeed the cause of the above fail. Thanks!
But still, what about moving files to trash instead of completely removing them? This will not solve this particular issue, but it will at least save our files if another similar issue happens.
"Trash" will not be supported. However, #218 was added a few seconds ago, which when enabled will make removes simply move the file to an archive.

Sure, that is even better! However, what do you mean by "move the file to an archive"? How is it implemented exactly? Could you be so kind to document it somewhere?
Don't get me wrong, I know that you have a lot of stuff to do, I really appreciate all this amazing effort. But just asking for some clarification about this feature :)
Give me a few seconds to write the blog post first... :) See the new comment at the end of #218.
Personally I see retaining deleted items as a separate concern which will be handled by my file manager. I would rather syncthing didn't use more disc space than necessary.
Don't enable versioning.
That works lol
Woo, thanks for the patch! Let me know if you want me test another release at some point.

Just updated to v0.8.21 and I can confirm it now refuses to proceed if it detects a symlink root. The error "stopped" is perhaps a little unclear but it's no longer destructive which is a huge improvement
